Apache.et: From Spanish apache, likely in part through English Apache. Further origin uncertain; possibly from Zuni ˀa˙paču.
From French apache, itself after the tribe above.

s: unusual and distinctive in an appealing way; featuring an exciting mixture of traits or influences
apart.et: 16th century, from Middle French à part (“separately”). The modern sense follows the French attributive use as in une chose à part (“something of its kind, something exceptional”).

s: apartheid (South African policy of racial segregation and discrimination)
apartheid, segregation (policy or situation of separation and discrimination based on a specified attribute)

On some still not precisely determined and quite recently discovered minerals. I count among these the following three substances: 1. the apatite of Mr. Werner. […]
Apatit.et: Coined by the German geologist Abraham Gottlob Werner (1749–1817) from Ancient Greek ᾰ̓πᾰ́τη (ăpắtē, “deceit, fraud”) as it is often mistaken for other minerals (possibly from Pre-Greek) + -it (suffix forming nouns denoting minerals or rocks).

s: an unusual but attractive trait or quality; see German apart for further definition

Hier und da, wie im episch wirkenden „Fall In Love, Fall Apart“, bricht die betörende Ruhe auf und lässt ein regelrechtes Arrangement-Gewitter zu.

t: Was ist Apathie? Sicher nichts Weltbewegendes.
What is apathy? Certainly nothing earth-shaking.

Apathy is a paralysis of the soul, an early death.
l: Auch ein stark gesteigerter Antrieb genau wie - gegenteilig dazu - totale Apathie könnten auf ein Höhenhirnödem hinweisen.
